sonnet.problem: Card 11 asks a true/false question about verse 10, but the card before it (card 10) only told verse 9, and the story card that tells verses 10-11 comes after the question (card 12). Nothing the baker has seen lets them reason out whether the oppressed 'also ask where God their Maker is', so it is a 50/50 luck guess. Card 12 then tells the answer afterwards.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: Verses 6 and 7 are parallel lines making one point: neither sin nor righteousness gives God anything. Card 7 already asked that point (sin cannot harm God), so card 8 asks it again about righteousness. The statement also adds that God receives something 'He needs', which verse 7 does not say.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.
